correctness.rationale: Normalize the common nonzero singular value to one. For input/output overlaps c,d the squared singular values have product (1-c²)(1-d²) and trace maximized at 2+2cd by aligning the phases. At fixed product their p/2-power sum increases strictly in trace (differentiate for unequal positive eigenvalues and use continuity or the one-nonzero-eigenvalue formula at the boundary). Real two-dimensional vectors realize every aligned c,d. Setting c=tanh z and d=tanh w reduces the conditional log derivative in w to a positive factor times tanh((p/2)(z+w))-tanh w, so the interior maximum is w=kz; c=0 or 1 can only give an optimum of one. The reduced objective H has H>1 for finite z>0 by strict convexity of log cosh and the exact weighted-mean relation, and tends to one at both ends. Its derivative changes sign where the ratio of integrals of sech²(az) over [1,p] and [p,k] crosses one. The ratio is strictly increasing because the ratio of these integrands at z₂>z₁ strictly decreases with a; its limits are 1/k and infinity by the dominant lower endpoints. This checks existence, uniqueness and all equality conditions in the stated class. With ε=p-1, expand the derivative bracket to 2ε²z sech²(z)(1-z tanh z)+O(ε³) on compact intervals and bracket its root at z₀. The second-order log-objective term is ε²z² sech²(z)/2, yielding (z₀²-1)/2; an independent scalar bisection gave 0.2196144199453. The Hilbert endpoint also follows without tracking z: the aligned squared quotient converges uniformly on [0,1]² to (1+cd)/(1+c²), whose unique maximum is at c=√2-1,d=1. Compactness then gives convergence of both maximizers and the optimal constant. Frozen verification code was inspected, not run; the reported finite tests do not certify the universal optimization. No unrestricted low-p sharp bound follows.
